I could not verify this against the literature, so the answer below is a best estimate from partial recall and a plausible lower-bound argument, not a derivation.

**Lower bound.** $K_4$ has treewidth 3, so $t(3) \ge \chi_l^{\star}(K_4)$. I recall that $\chi_l^{\star}(K_n) = 2n-1$ for $n$ at least 3 (I'm not certain of the exact range), which would give $\chi_l^{\star}(K_4) = 7$ and hence $t(3) \ge 7$.

**Upper bound.** I recall, without confidence, a result that graphs of treewidth at most $d$ satisfy $\chi_l^{\star} \le 2d+1$, which would give $t(3) \le 7$ and make the bound tight. I could not reconstruct a proof of this upper bound here.

Combining these gives $t(3) = 7$, but both bounds rest on recollection rather than verified proofs.

ANSWER: 7
